- Use nested classes in `@layer components` for styling parents and children elements
- Create a new component in `srs/components` root directory
- Never touch the files in `srs/components/ui` directory

content.value_statement: Tailwind CSS component work often needs consistent project rules and file placement. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise rules for Tailwind component styling.
actual_capabilities: Guides agents to create separate CSS files for component styling.
Directs use of Tailwind apply, layer, utility, and variant directives.
Points agents to project Tailwind v4.1 context documents when available.
Encourages nested component styles inside the components layer.
Defines component placement under the project components directory.
Protects the UI component directory from edits.
limitations: It only covers Tailwind CSS component styling guidance.
It depends on local Tailwind context files that may not exist in every project.
It does not install Tailwind CSS or verify project dependencies.
The source text contains a directory typo, so agents may need human confirmation.

use_cases.title: Create Project Components
use_cases.description: Build a new Tailwind styled component while following local directory and styling rules.

use_cases.title: Standardize Styling Patterns
use_cases.description: Keep component CSS consistent across a team by reusing the same Tailwind directive patterns.

use_cases.title: Update Existing UI Safely
use_cases.description: Apply Tailwind component styles while avoiding protected shared UI files.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Tailwind CSS component for a profile card. Follow the project styling rules from this skill.

prompt_templates.title: Style an Existing Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this component with a separate CSS file. Use Tailwind component layer patterns and keep shared UI files unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Use Tailwind v4 Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the available Tailwind v4.1 context documents, then style this component using the documented project patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Component Styling
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor these related components into consistent Tailwind component styles. Use utilities and variants where the project rules support them.

output_examples.input: Create a notification banner with Tailwind CSS.
output_examples.output: The agent creates a component and a matching CSS file, then applies Tailwind component layer styles for the banner states.

output_examples.input: Improve an existing settings panel without editing shared UI files.
output_examples.output: The agent keeps protected UI files unchanged and places new styling in the allowed component area.

output_examples.input: Align a new card component with Tailwind v4 project rules.
output_examples.output: The agent reviews local Tailwind context files when present and follows the documented directive patterns.

best_practices: Confirm the correct components directory before creating files.
Review local Tailwind context documents before large styling changes.
Keep shared UI components unchanged unless the user explicitly approves edits.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill for general backend or database work.
Do not assume missing Tailwind context documents exist.
Do not edit protected shared UI files without explicit user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It guides AI agents when creating or updating Tailwind CSS components.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it install Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: No. It provides styling guidance and does not run dependency installation.

faq.question: Does it execute shell commands?
faq.answer: No evidence of shell command execution was found in SKILL.md.

faq.question: Why mention Tailwind v4.1 documents?
faq.answer: The skill tells agents to use local project context documents when those files are available.

faq.question: Can it modify shared UI components?
faq.answer: The skill instructs agents not to touch the shared UI components directory.
